newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: HORSE RACING-CIPISEK WINS GRAND PARDUBICE IN RECORD TIME.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-CIPISEK WINS GRAND PARDUBICE IN RECORD TIME.

text.p: Local horse Cipisek, ridden by Vladislav Snitkovskij, won the 106th Grand Pardubice steeplechase on Sunday, outpacing the field with a strong final run to outpace the field and set a new course record.
Eight-year-old Cipisek was an outsider at 15-to-one but completed the four-and-a-quarter mile (6.9 km) race in a record nine minutes 35 seconds to earn the one million crown ($36,900) purse.
Snitkovskij, who won the race in 1994 on Czech horse Erudit, came on strongly as last year's winner and this year's favourite It's a Snip faded in the last half mile after leading much of the way.

Finishing second some four-and-a-half lengths behind was one of a trio of British horses at the race, Irish Stamp, ridden by Norman Williamson. It's a Snip, with England's Richard Dunwoody in the saddle, finished third.

The Pardubice is a demanding 32-jump race which includes the notorious Taxis jump. a high and wide fence with a deep ditch which was modified after an embarrassing 1993 outcome when only one horse managed to finish.
Czech horse Galaxy, which had thrown its rider early in a preliminary race, attempted to jump the Taxis, fell and was put down, becoming the 22nd horse to die in the meeting's history.

Animal rights activists, including former French film actress Brigitte Bardot, have protested against the race in the past. But fears that largescale demonstrations would marr this year's race did not materialise.
Ten of the 21 starters completed the race, although a huge gap separated the top three finishers from the rest of the field.
